findings.description: Replay is not byte-for-byte for half the corpus already checked in, and nothing notices. `replay` puts the recorded document into `Response.Structured`, and `writeStream` (internal/claudesim/stream.go:106-109) assigns it to `event.StructuredOutput json.RawMessage` and emits the event with `json.Marshal` (stream.go:113). `json.Marshal` runs a RawMessage through `compact` with escapeHTML=true, so every `<`, `>` and `&` in the recorded bytes is rewritten as `<`, `>`, `&`. Two of the four seeded entries contain those characters: `dialogue-fixes-second-look` has "round 1 < Cap" and `dialogue-layer-second-look` has "round 1 < Cap", "--detach <path>", "&&" and the trailing `</risk_level>`. So a scenario stating `recorded: dialogue-fixes-second-look` emits a document that is not the recorded one, socrates stores the escaped form in findings.json, and the byte comparisons in internal/claudesim/replay_test.go:29 and internal/e2e/journeys_test.go:113 would fail. They pass today only because both tests happen to name `dialogue-layer-first-look`, the entry with no such character. The escaping is silent (the escaped JSON parses to the same document, so routing is identical), and it will bite every future recorded answer that quotes a comparison or a tag, which the raw `<` in the seed shows the real CLI does not escape on its way in. Emitting the result event with a `json.Encoder` whose `SetEscapeHTML(false)` is set, or writing the structured field verbatim, closes it; a test over every entry rather than one named constant is what would have caught it.

The model and effort an entry is recorded with are taken from the *last* `agent-started`/`reviewer` event in the whole run log, not from the round being recorded, and the event carries no round number. Concrete path: a run parks at round 1 (reviewed by whatever `internal/config` resolved then), the author edits the roles block of the config, `scrat continue` runs round 2 in a fresh process with `model: sonnet`, and a second `agent-started` event is appended (internal/agent/claude.go:133-141). `corpus-record -run R -round 1` then takes base and snapshot from round 1 (runs.go:65-66) but overwrites `routing["model"]` with round 2's value at runs.go:97, and records the round-one answer as sonnet's. Nothing errors: the entry validates, the report classifies it, and the corpus now attributes an answer to a model that never produced it, which the specification calls the circumstance without which the answer "is not evidence of anything". A second path to the same wrong answer is log rotation: `runlog.Writer` truncates at 1 MiB and keeps only the tail (internal/runlog/writer.go:90-131), so an early round's `agent-started` can be gone while a later one's survives. Fixing it needs the round on the event, or a refusal to record a round whose own `agent-started` cannot be identified.

Recording accepts an answer that socrates never routed, including one that is not a findings document, and the resulting entry breaks the whole suite rather than the recording. `Answered` never looks at `run.State` and never parses the document, and `corpus.Record`'s only check on the bytes is `len(e.Document) == 0` (internal/corpus/corpus.go:111). Concrete path: a review returns `{"findings":"none that matter","risk_level":"low","risk_rationale":"r"}` (the simulator's `schema-violation`, or any real answer that fails `findings.Validate`); supervise.go:112-116 writes findings.json because the structured field is non-empty, then `findings.Parse` fails at supervise.go:143 and the run ends `failed`. `corpus-record -run R -round 1 -name x -subject y` then succeeds and prints "recorded x". From that commit on, `outcomes.Of` fails at internal/corpus/outcomes/outcomes.go:30-33, so `make corpus-outcomes` exits 2 and both `TestTheRecordedDistributionMatchesTheCorpus` and `TestAnEntryHoldsTheAnswerAndItsCircumstances` fail on an unrelated change, while the command that created the state reported success. Parsing the document in `Record` (or refusing a run that reached no routed outcome) puts the refusal where the operator is.

The name guard rejects `/`, `\` and exactly `..`, but not the names that `//go:embed answers` silently drops. `corpus-record -name .first-look` writes internal/corpus/answers/.first-look/{answer,entry}.json and prints "recorded", yet Go's embed patterns exclude files and directories whose names begin with `.` or `_`, so `corpus.Entries()` never sees it: it is absent from replay, from the report and from distribution.txt, and no test or gate notices because the distribution is unchanged. `-name .` is worse: `filepath.Join` collapses it to the answers directory itself, so answer.json and entry.json land in the corpus root where `read` skips them (corpus.go:136), and the command still reports success. Rejecting a leading `.` or `_` and a name that is not a single path element closes both.

The report's second number is a count of test functions that *mention* a state, not of scenarios that assert the outcome, and it is printed as "%d asserted by the suite" (internal/corpus/outcomes/outcomes.go:69) under a claim in AGENTS.md that it is "how many scenarios in the suite assert it". `statesNamedIn` collects any `runstate.X` selector or matching string literal anywhere inside a `Test*` function, so internal/exit/code_test.go:10 `TestEachVerdictHasItsOwnCode` (a map from state to exit code) is counted as asserting both `clean` and `escalated`, `TestFailureIsNotEscalation` at code_test.go:24 is counted for `escalated`, and internal/snapshot/content_test.go and internal/runstore/sweep_test.go contribute similarly. Tests that assert a run must *not* reach a state count as asserting it, subtests are not counted at all, and the outcomes package's own tests are counted. So the one column that is supposed to tell a reader how much of an outcome's coverage is hand-written can move without any coverage changing, and can be high for an outcome nothing routes to. Either narrow what counts as an assertion or label the column as mentions.

The only guard on that count cannot fail. `named == 0` is computed from `outcomes.Asserting(source.Root(t))`, which walks this very file; `TestTheReportCountsWhatItClassified` itself names `runstate.Escalated` (line 65) and `TestAnOutcomeNoReviewerHasReachedIsNamed` names `runstate.AwaitingResponse` (line 88), so `named >= 2` for as long as the test exists, whatever `Asserting` does to every other file. The check at lines 65-67 is likewise subsumed by the loop at 60-64, since `escalated` is in `reachable`. Related: because the AST walk lives in a non-test package, `TestSocratesHoldsItselfToTheTestQualityRule` does not see it - `TestsReadingGoFiles` only inspects `_test.go` paths (internal/convention/evidence.go:57) - so a test whose evidence about the suite is a parse of the suite's source enters the repository without an entry in `ContractsTestsRead`, which is the one gate written to stop exactly that. Exercising `Asserting` against a fabricated tree, as internal/convention/evidence_test.go:33 does for its own rule, would make the claim falsifiable.

The `// scenario: A live review's answer is kept` marker claims a scenario about the real binary for a test that runs against the simulator. The requirement it belongs to is "The simulator is checked against the real tool", and the scenario reads "WHEN a live review against the real binary returns a findings document" (openspec/changes/what-a-reviewer-actually-answered/specs/agent-seam/spec.md:52-55); this test calls `harness.Start`, sets `escalatingScenario` and reviews a repository whose go.mod is written by the test purely to satisfy the socrates-only guard. `coverage.Gaps` matches on normalised text alone, so `make scenario-coverage` now reports that scenario as covered while task 6.4 ("One live run, recorded into the corpus") is still open, and archiving the change would promote the requirement as satisfied by a simulated run. A test that is genuinely worth having, but the scenario it claims is the one this change says a live run must satisfy.

risk_rationale:
Nothing in the shipped `scrat` binary changes behaviour, so the blast radius is test infrastructure and the corpus itself, but the headline invariant (byte-for-byte replay) is already false for two of the four seeded entries and holds in the suite only by the choice of one test constant, and two recording paths write wrong or unroutable evidence without erroring.</risk_level>
</invoke>
